name: the hydra
description: Chess with a monster in the middle of the board. A hydra stands on d4 and another on d5, and neither ever walks; instead, any piece that ends its owner's move attacking a hydra, pawns included, is eaten at once by a new head that grows onto its square. A head is a hydra in every way, so the monster spreads along the lines its attackers came from, and a head grown on your piece's square can be taken at once by an enemy piece that was guarding that square: feeding the hydra is an exchange, and a sacrifice that opens a line can be one too. No more than six heads may stand at once; past that, a head lunges onto the piece that attacks it instead, and leaves its post. A hydra cannot harm a king, so the king is the one piece that may walk up to a head and take it, and the king becomes the hydra-slayer. Four hounds walk short three-square loops on the wings, and after every move a hound takes a piece of the player who has just moved that stands next to it, then waits where it landed until it can pounce again or finds itself back on a loop; the hounds by Black's camp walk one move behind those by White's, so each army meets the hounds at its door after its own second move. So the centre is a minefield in which a careless knight or a long-range piece feeds the monster, and the question all game is when to open lines through the middle, and when to send the king to clear it. Checkmate wins; a game that reaches its move limit, or fifty moves a side without a capture or a promotion, goes to the side with more material.

provenance.source: docs/plan-npc.md, N7: the showcase for pounce on prey, pounce on attackers and split (section 6.2)
provenance.history: Section 6.2 of docs/plan-npc.md, pre-registered 2026-10-25 before any of its rules was built: chess with a stationary hydra pair on d4 and d5 that takes what attacks it (every type but the king) and splits up to six heads, and four hounds on three-square wing loops that take the mover's pieces next to them. Registered after a draft read in self-play at 1600 and 6400 nodes, with the one tunable the read argued for moved: the loops keep their squares, start on b4 and g4, and the black side's run one ply behind the white side's (four entries in place of two mirrored ones), because a mirrored pair starts both sides' hounds on the same ply and the drafted start took two of the first player's pawns on its first move whatever it played.
